headline: NEWMONT SMASHES Q3 ESTIMATES — Record $2.3B Adj Net Income, EPS $2.20 vs $1.96 Est; AISC $1,454 Beats $1,520 Guidance
snippet: Newmont Corporation (NYSE: NEM) reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted net income of $2.3 billion ($2.20 per diluted share) after the close on October 22, beating the $1.96 consensus estimate and marking a record Q3 result. Gold by-product all-in sustaining costs came in at $1,454 per ounce — $66 below the midpoint of full-year $1,520 guidance — while free cash flow reached $1.9 billion and net cash stood at $3.2 billion before a planned $1.95 billion Nevada Gold Mines payment to Barrick in Q4. Production was 1.3 million attributable gold ounces; full-year guidance of 5.3 million ounces was reaffirmed. The release also included a Red Chris block cave update and a $0.26 per-share dividend, setting up Q4 as the strongest quarter and establishing AISC improvement as the key variable for junior investors tracking major-miner cost benchmarks.

headline: GOLD PIERCES $4,100 FLOOR — $4,084 as Silver Tumbles 3.5% to $55.94; Brent Near $112 and Oct 27-28 FOMC Now Make-or-Break
snippet: Spot gold fell $56.40 to $4,084 per ounce on October 22 — piercing the $4,100 support level in a fifth consecutive losing session — while silver dropped $2.04 to $55.94, a decline of 3.52%. Brent crude holding near $112 per barrel keeps Treasury yields above 5.1% and sustains pricing of roughly 17% odds of a Federal Reserve hike at the October 27–28 FOMC meeting; that combination leaves non-yielding gold exposed to further selling if oil does not pull back before the decision. For junior mining investors, the $4,100 breach is the most significant technical support failure since gold's spring consolidation; the Newmont Q3 beat after the close provides an operational earnings counter-narrative, but macro pressure will dominate until the FOMC outcome.

headline: COPPER HITS FIVE-WEEK LOW AT $14,089/T — LME Inventory Build Continues; U.S. Warehouses Now Hold 62% of Global LME Stocks
snippet: LME three-month copper fell 1.8% to $14,089 per tonne on October 22, its lowest level in five weeks, as warehouse inventories continued to build and U.S. stocks consolidated their hold on approximately 62% of all LME copper inventory. The ongoing accumulation signals that near-term demand is not keeping pace with the supply that reached exchange warehouses following the BHP-Escondida labour resolution and easing Chilean weather constraints. The ICSG's 2026 refined surplus forecast of 104,000 tonnes — widening further in 2027 — is increasingly reflected in the price, though the 17-year mine development pipeline gap means the structural deficit thesis for the early 2030s is intact.

headline: K2 GOLD MOJAVE DRILLS 83.82m AT 3.40 G/T FROM SURFACE — Dragonfly Includes 19.81m AT 7.58 G/T; Clean $33.9M Treasury, No Warrants
snippet: K2 Gold (TSX-V: KTO) released final first-phase results from the Dragonfly Zone at its Mojave Project in California's Mojave Desert, with the highlight hole returning 83.82 metres at 3.40 g/t gold from surface — including 48.77 metres at 4.98 g/t from 35.05 metres and 19.81 metres at 7.58 g/t from 64.01 metres. The result extends a high-grade surface-to-depth gold system at a BLM-permitted project that K2 is advancing toward a second drilling phase. K2 carries $33.9 million in treasury with no warrants outstanding — a capital structure well-suited to attracting an acquirer given the 2026 California gold M&A cycle, with the Gold Valley target 1.5 kilometres along strike still untested.

headline: LIBERTY GOLD OPENS 50,000m SEASON AT BLACK PINE IDAHO — 2026 Initial 29 Holes Hit 62.5m AT 0.42 G/T; Rangefront Oxide Zone Extends North
snippet: Liberty Gold (TSX: LGD) reported initial results from its 50,000-metre 2026 drill program at Black Pine in Cassia County, Idaho — 7,417 metres in 29 reverse circulation holes extending the Rangefront oxide zone northward, with the best intercept of 62.5 metres at 0.42 g/t gold including 0.63 g/t over 15.2 metres. The Rangefront area was discovered in the 2025 season when hole LBP1197 returned 123.4 metres at 0.86 g/t; the 2026 expanded program is building the data density for a resource classification upgrade ahead of a pre-feasibility study on this heap-leach-amenable, open-pittable oxide system in a permitting-constructive Idaho county.

headline: ALPHA EXPLORATION DRILLS 37% OVER TARGET AT ABURNA ERITREA — 8,910m Completed vs 6,500m Plan; Northeast Prospect Resource Estimate Next
snippet: Alpha Exploration (TSXV: ALEX) completed its 2026 drill campaign at the Aburna Gold Project in Eritrea with 8,910 metres finished — approximately 37% above the fully-funded 6,500-metre plan — after expanding the program to follow up on encouraging results across four of seven new targets in the Aburna corridor. The October 6 batch had highlighted 7 metres at 7.09 g/t gold within 19 metres at 3.18 g/t at the Northeast Prospect; the company notes that approximately 20% of the multi-kilometre Aburna corridor has been systematically drilled to date, leaving substantial upside for the maiden resource estimate expected following receipt of final-batch assays.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD RELEASES FRESH GOLD ROCK ASSAYS — Two Rigs Active at Ontario Camp; Mud Lake North Holes Awaiting Results
snippet: Dryden Gold (TSXV: DRY) released additional assays from its ongoing drill campaign at the Gold Rock Gold System near Dryden, Ontario, where a second rig was added in July 2026 to accelerate testing of the Big Master, Jubilee, Pearl, and Elora high-grade zones. The September batch had highlighted hole DGR-058 returning 7.88 g/t gold over 12.70 metres at the Jubilee-Pearl intersection; the latest release continues to build the deposit's strike length and grade-thickness model ahead of an updated resource estimate. Three holes from the new Mud Lake North target — located 3 kilometres north of Gold Rock — are also awaiting assay results that could extend the camp's footprint.

headline: MONEY METALS: SILVER BULL MARKET ISN'T OVER — 'Setting Up for Next Leg Higher' After 53% Collapse From $121 January Record
snippet: Money Metals Exchange's October 22 market commentary argues that silver's collapse from its January 2026 record near $121 per ounce to the current $55–56 range — a 53% drawdown in nine months — is a sentiment reset driven by oil-fuelled rate fears, not a fundamental breakdown in the bull case. The analysis highlights that the gold-silver ratio has widened back toward 70–72 in October after trading below 50 in January: a level that has historically marked maximum silver underperformance within a secular precious metals bull market. With the FOMC decision on October 27–28 serving as the near-term clearing event, the piece positions current silver prices as an accumulation zone, not a signal to exit.

headline: IS USA RARE EARTH A ONCE-IN-A-GENERATION BUY? — USAR Down 74% From Peak; Reshoring Thesis Tightens as China Decoupling Accelerates
snippet: Motley Fool's October 22 analysis examines USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) — down 74% from its October 2025 lifetime high and roughly 15% year-to-date — as a potential multi-year re-entry point for investors positioned on US reshoring and China decoupling. The company completed a CEO transition on October 1 and is awaiting milestone-based US government funding decisions expected by year-end, creating a binary near-term catalyst. China's export restriction policy on rare earth magnets has created structural urgency for domestic US rare earth processing capacity, and with USAR's stock deeply discounted from its IPO-era highs, the gap between strategic necessity and current market pricing is the core argument the piece makes.

headline: SILVER'S DUAL MANDATE: FIVE REASONS INDUSTRIAL + MONETARY DEMAND CONVERGE IN 2026 — FXStreet Analysis as Price Hits April Low
snippet: An FXStreet analysis published October 21 maps five demand channels for silver that operate independently of monetary policy: solar panel silver paste consumption (growing with each 100 GW of new capacity), EV power electronics, industrial electrical contacts and conductors, monetary and ETF accumulation, and FOMC-sensitive speculative positioning. The piece argues the first four are structural and accelerating regardless of near-term rate decisions, while the fifth — speculative outflows driven by oil-inflation-rate fears — is pushing silver to its lowest since April 2026 at $56. For junior silver explorers and developers, the framework provides an analytical template for how silver demand re-rates once the rate-fear cycle peaks, potentially creating a sharper recovery than gold in the post-FOMC window.
